Checked description/order_no fields too -- no free-text bank narrative exists anywhere in the DB for this era. VERDICT UNCHANGED: the R54,902.41 orphaned cash remains UNRESOLVED. monthly_lpg_insights.csv NOT updated -- no valid change found. This closes off the last ERP-internal lead with a concrete disproof rather than an absence of a match, reinforcing (not just repeating) the existing recommendation that only an external bank statement/bordereau can resolve this. Investigated 2024 Sept/Oct/Nov (R41,887.32, flagged unresolved in the previous entry). Tested the 'six payments cleared eight months, Apr-Nov 2024' pooled-window claim directly: ran a full-year FIFO simulation, applying every 2024 payment's REAL gross (not the CSV's per-month-capped figures) in strict payment-date order against every month's billing in date order. It DOES mathematically resolve to exactly zero residual across all 12 months, using only cash already on file -- looks like it vindicates the pooled-window claim at first. REJECTED on a lag-plausibility check: built a proper baseline from every confirmed single-payment 2024 month (100-190 days, trending UPWARD across the year, consistent with a widening collections gap) -- the full FIFO reconstruction requires Sept/Oct/Nov's implied lag to suddenly DROP to 43-80 days, then jump back to ~141 days by December. No plausible business reason for that dip. Same category of mechanical-fill artifact already ruled out elsewhere on this account (business_rules.md SS3) -- a zero residual isn't diagnostic once total cash exceeds total need over a long enough window; some ordering was always going to tie out. VERDICT: Sept/Oct/Nov 2024 (R41,887.32) are genuinely UNPAID, real current exposure, NOT a pooled-window artifact. Updated JIM001_Legal_Handoff_Investigation_Tasks.md: moved this from Priority 3 (historical, not part of current claim) into Priority 1 (the actual claim) -- title changed to '2024, 2025 & 2026 unpaid invoices'. Bridge review SS5.2 added with the full lag-baseline table and rejection reasoning. SS5.2's verdict survives only in its narrower form (a sustained 3-month regime dip, not a single-month flag) and is ASSERTED, not proven.
